title: Direct cueing of word identity through word duration: evidence from Mandarin homophones
abstract: arXiv:2610.30682v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While there is increasing evidence that words are stored in the mental lexicon with some phonetic detail, there are open questions about exactly which phonetic details are stored and whether they are functionally relevant for spoken word recognition. Word-level phonetic cues, such as word duration, provide an appropriate test case. Across languages, including Mandarin Chinese, high frequency words are shorter than low frequency words. Using a homophone ordering task, we investigate whether differences in word duration impact word recognition. Mandarin Chinese was examined since it has abundant disyllabic homophones. Our results indicate that participants were able to use word duration to recognize the order of homophone pairs, selected to vary in lexical frequency. Both with high noise levels and when no other cues were available, participants mapped the shorter duration auditory stimulus to the higher frequency word. The results provide

translated_title: 通过词长直接提示词的身份：来自汉语同音词的证据
translated_abstract: 越来越多的证据表明，词汇在心理词典中以包含一定语音细节的形式存储，但关于究竟存储了哪些语音细节，以及这些细节在口语词汇识别中是否具有功能性作用，仍存在未解决的问题。词汇层面的语音线索（如词长）为此提供了一个合适的测试案例。在包括汉语在内的多种语言中，高频词比低频词更短。我们采用同音词排序任务，考察词长差异是否会影响词汇识别。之所以选择汉语进行研究，是因为汉语拥有大量的双音节同音词。结果表明，被试能够利用词长来识别同音词对的顺序，这些同音词对是按照词汇频率差异筛选的。无论是在高噪声条件下，还是在没有其他线索可用的情况下，被试都会将时长较短的听觉刺激映射到频率较高的词上。这些结果表明……
tldr: 本研究通过汉语同音词排序任务发现，听者能够利用词长（高频词更短）这一语音线索直接识别词的身份，证明词长在口语词汇识别中具有功能性作用。
en_tdlr: Using a Mandarin homophone ordering task, this study shows that listeners directly use word duration as a cue to word identity, mapping shorter stimuli to higher-frequency words, demonstrating that word duration is functionally relevant for spoken word recognition.
